subject.title: docs: propose plugin-owned external verification approvals

question: Should OpenClaw accept this registration-derived, attempt-bound plugin attestation contract as the permanent core seam for external approval verification?
rationale: The RFC deliberately lets plugin code attest an external ceremony that can unblock protected execution; automation cannot choose that durable trust and compatibility boundary.

options.title: Validate and accept the narrow seam
options.body: Keep the revised ownership model, require approval-boundary review plus prototype-aligned proof, and accept the RFC once those checks confirm the contract.

options.title: Require a prototype before acceptance
options.body: Leave the RFC in draft until a current implementation demonstrates the revised identity, compatibility, replay, and denial semantics.

options.title: Reject external resolution in core
options.body: Keep plugin approvals limited to existing decisions and require external verifiers to use a separate plugin-owned workflow without protected-call continuation.

recommendation.title: Validate and accept the narrow seam
recommendation.body: Keep the revised ownership model, require approval-boundary review plus prototype-aligned proof, and accept the RFC once those checks confirm the contract.

likelyOwner.reason: They are actively reviewing the exact API, compatibility, and approval semantics that require a human decision.
